scenario: Two mountain-rescue teams, Sierra and Nordic, are assessed on successful rescue completion rates. Team Sierra is predominantly dispatched to severe high-altitude incidents; Team Nordic handles mostly low-altitude moderate incidents.

data.description: rescue completion rates by incident severity and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate rescue completion rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each incident severity stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 incident severity mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: Team Nordic's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier moderate cases. Team Sierra outperforms Team Nordic in both incident severity strata. Standardising to a 50/50 incident severity mix gives Team Sierra 0.835 vs Team Nordic 0.795; Team Sierra is the superior performer once incident severity is controlled.

naive_answer: Team Nordic is better because its aggregate rescue completion rate (0.8771) exceeds Team Sierra's (0.7671).
naive_trap: Incident severity is a confounder: Team Sierra handles the majority of harder severe cases, depressing its aggregate while Team Nordic benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Severe: Team Sierra 0.74 > Team Nordic 0.68. (2) Moderate: Team Sierra 0.93 > Team Nordic 0.91. (3) Team Sierra handles 85.7% severe cases vs Team Nordic's 14.3% — this pulls Team Sierra's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: Team Sierra=0.5×0.74+0.5×0.93=0.835; Team Nordic=0.5×0.68+0.5×0.91=0.795. Team Sierra wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 600,0.74,100,0.93
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.68,600,0.91
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: Team Nordic aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.835)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.795)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: Team Sierra wins'
